hero.headline: Turn a body of work into a system that can remember, disagree, mature, and repair itself.
hero.support: A research-operations method for transforming notes, documents, conversations, models, experiments, and revisions into a traceable corpus with provenance, explicit claim status, contradiction handling, review gates, and replacement history.

primaryCta.label: Trace a claim through the forge

definition.title: A corpus is not a pile of documents. It is a governed memory system.
definition.body: Corpus Forge treats sources, extracted claims, relationships, contradictions, reviews, promotions, and supersessions as distinct objects so later synthesis can remain reconstructable instead of silently flattening everything into current prose.
definition.rule: Compression is allowed only when the path back to consequential source, status, disagreement, and replacement history remains available.

lifecycle.title: Six stages from source to durable corpus.

stages.name: 1. Ingest
stages.question: What is the source, where did it come from, and what boundary must remain attached to it?

stages.name: 2. Extract
stages.question: Which claims, concepts, artifacts, questions, evidence references, and candidate relationships are present?

stages.name: 3. Relate
stages.question: What supports, contradicts, depends on, refines, duplicates, or supersedes what?

stages.name: 4. Review
stages.question: Which extraction or synthesis decisions require a human witness before they can become durable?

stages.name: 5. Promote
stages.question: Which bounded objects have enough evidence and review to enter a stronger maturity state?
stages.artifact: Promoted claim or artifact with status

stages.name: 6. Supersede / repair
stages.question: When new evidence changes the representation, what is replaced, what remains historical, and which downstream objects must be revisited?

types.name: Source
types.purpose: Preserve the original artifact and its provenance boundary.

types.name: Claim
types.purpose: Represent an assertion with explicit maturity, scope, and evidence links.

types.name: Evidence
types.purpose: Record observations, references, tests, or artifacts offered in support or tension.

types.name: Contradiction
types.purpose: Preserve disagreement as an object to resolve or retain, not noise to average away.

types.name: Decision
types.purpose: Attribute consequential review, promotion, rejection, or repair choices.

types.name: Supersession
types.purpose: Record that a newer representation replaces another for a declared purpose without deleting history.

workedExample.title: Illustrative trace: when a design claim and an incident disagree.
workedExample.setup: Suppose a design note says a retryable command is idempotent, while a later incident review records duplicate execution after a timeout and retry. A conventional summary may simply update the prose. Corpus Forge keeps the disagreement inspectable.

trace.state: The design note and incident review remain separate source records with dates, authorship/provenance, and their original language preserved.
Candidate claim A: the command is idempotent. Candidate claim B: a timeout/retry path produced duplicate execution.
The corpus records tension between the claims rather than forcing early reconciliation. Logs, tests, code versions, or reproduction artifacts can attach as evidence.
A reviewer determines whether the claims concern the same version, execution path, environment, or definition of idempotence and records the decision basis.
Only the bounded finding supported by the reviewed evidence is promoted. Unresolved scope remains explicit.
If the earlier design claim is no longer admissible for the current system, it is superseded rather than erased, and dependent summaries or claims enter a repair queue.

workedExample.lesson: The goal is not to preserve every sentence forever. It is to preserve enough structure that a consequential claim can be reconstructed, challenged, replaced, and repaired without inventing history.
workedExample.scopeNote: This is a constructed research-operations example, not a report about a specific production system.

promotionGrammar.title: Maturity is a state transition, not a formatting choice.
gates: supporting and contradicting evidence is represented
replacement and repair obligations are visible

validation.title: A governed corpus should be testable as an information system.
targets: reconstruct a public claim back to material sources and review decisions
detect when contradictory evidence exists but has not been resolved
prevent lower-maturity notes from silently appearing as established claims
recover why a superseded representation existed and what replaced it
identify downstream objects affected by a repaired or withdrawn claim
measure human review burden introduced by stronger provenance and promotion gates
validation.claimRule: Corpus Forge is in active development. These are operational goals and validation targets, not published reliability or productivity results.

relationship.title: Method, software, and focused surfaces remain distinct.
relationship.workbench: Corpus Forge Workbench is a maintained software/product expression of this method and program. Its retained landing record is not currently promoted as a public route.
relationship.ledger: Claim and Evidence Ledger is a focused product surface extracted from the wider governance model.
relationship.boundary: The public Corpus Forge page describes the research-operations program. It should not imply that every planned software capability is deployed, validated, or publicly available.

claimBoundary.title: Active development, not a claim of solved knowledge management.
safe: Corpus Forge is a current Boundary First Labs research-operations method and software-development program.
Its core design objective is reconstructable provenance, maturity, disagreement, review, supersession, and repair.
Individual mechanisms can be compared with established provenance systems, knowledge graphs, version control, scholarly workflows, data lineage, argument mapping, and research information systems.
notEstablished: that Corpus Forge is a complete or production-ready knowledge-management platform
that the method eliminates hallucination, disagreement, stale knowledge, or review error
that stronger provenance necessarily reduces total research cost
that AI extraction can safely promote consequential claims without attributable human review where such review is required

closing.title: Let knowledge change without pretending it never changed.
closing.finalLine: Preserve the source. Extract the object. Keep disagreement visible. Promote deliberately. Record replacement. Repair what depended on the old claim.
